sources.entry: naming by GlacierPhonk - A Claude Code skill for naming products, SaaS tools, brands, and projects via a structured metaphor-driven process — naming brief, metaphor exploration, candidate generation, anti-slop filtering, a weighted evaluation rubric, and availability checks for domains/handles/package names. A genuinely different (and creative) take that produces names grounded in meaning instead

summary.one_liner: A Claude Code skill that walks Claude through a structured, metaphor-driven process for naming products, SaaS tools, brands, and projects while filtering out generic "AI-sounding" names.
summary.what_it_does: The skill guides Claude through seven steps: a naming brief, metaphor exploration, candidate generation, filtering of anti-patterns, weighted scoring of finalists, availability checks, and a final decision with origin stories and trade-offs. It is organized as a SKILL.md entry point plus about 14 reference files covering principles, phonosemantics (sound-meaning links), anti-patterns, metaphor mapping, cultural references, brand architecture, evaluation rubric, and foreign-word rules. A bundled shell script (scripts/check-availability.sh) checks domains, npm, GitHub, PyPI, and Telegram handles. Language and industry guides are included as indexed files, with Polish and Portuguese named in the README. The README says a quick session compresses the process automatically, while the reference files support deeper work.
use_cases: Naming a new product or SaaS tool
Brainstorming brand names with metaphor-based reasoning
Checking domain, handle, and package name availability for a candidate name
Scoring and comparing shortlisted names with a rubric
Naming projects within a brand family or product line
how_to_run: git clone <repo-url> .claude/skills/naming  (project skill, from project root)
In Claude Code, type /naming and describe what you need a name for in one sentence
notable: Metaphor-first process: maps conceptual territories before generating any names
Anti-slop filter targeting suffixes like -ly/-ify/-able, meaningless portmanteaus, and thesaurus extraction
Weighted evaluation rubric and decision checklist for comparing finalists
Bundled availability checker covering domains, npm, GitHub, PyPI, and Telegram
Modular reference files loaded on demand to limit context use
caveats: The README does not state platform limits or paid tiers beyond the Claude Code requirement
Availability checks depend on a bundled script; the README does not describe how reliable the results are
Language and industry coverage is limited to the files that exist; the README says new ones are welcome
